title: Returning to Normal: Getting Back on Track After a Focus Ultra (iRunFar, 2016)
population: One experienced ultrarunner's personal approach after the Hardrock 100
findings: First runs: some 25- to 45-minute light jogs on generally easy terrain.
Over the first week he adds days until running roughly two out of every three days, with runs kept to an hour or less.
He starts running on a normal schedule roughly the third week after a 100 miler.

Resets to roughly 8 hours of sleep a night about a week after the race; irregular sleep, seemingly random extremely low energy patches and signs of adrenal fatigue or overtraining syndrome are what he watches for.
limitations: Personal approach of one runner, presented as a baseline individuals should adjust; no data cited; the claim that volume stays below baseline in week 3 was not confirmed on re-fetch and is removed.
implications: Gives a ratio-style return: run about 2 of every 3 days by the end of week 1, 25 to 45 min early on, normal schedule about week 3.
Supports sleep disturbance and low-energy patches as check-in items to watch during the return; the page does not state what to do when they appear, so treat delay as the plan's own cautious choice.

verification.notes: Re-fetched the page (WebFetch): Bryon Powell, August 3, 2016; run lengths, 2-of-3 days, third-week normal schedule, 8 h sleep and warning signs confirmed. Removed 'volume still below baseline / no training efforts' and 'more days off' phrasings that the fetch did not confirm. The old URL (irunfar.com/2016/08/...html) now redirects to the stored one; the page is dated 2016-08-03 in its metadata. Practice source (programme, coaching or clinical page): a published convention, not evidence; grade D.

interests: Founding editor of iRunFar (the page carries an affiliate-link notice and gear reviews run on the site), author of two books and a coach (bio).

r1.note: The 25 to 45 minute first runs, running two days in three, runs of an hour or less, a normal schedule about the third week after a 100 miler with volume below baseline, about 8 hours of sleep and the warning signs located on the page fetched 2026-10-31 (published 2016-08-03, modified 2026-03-13).

r2.note: Author named (Bryon Powell). Hardrock's official results (read 2026-10-31) list him as a finisher in 2015 and 2016. He is the site's founding editor, so the publisher is not independent of him; the record is his own personal practice.

r3.note: Page modified 2026-03-13 after publication on 2016-08-03; the passage on returning to running is present in the version read. Later corpus papers (hoffman-2017, garciavaliente-2026) give no return protocol.

r4.note: The shape (short easy runs in the first week, a normal schedule from about week 3) agrees with Koop (cts-2025) and Roche (skurka-2017), independent coaches. One runner's personal approach, so the agreement is on shape, not on dose.

r5.note: Population is one experienced ultrarunner after the Hardrock 100, recorded as personal practice; the H12 notes label the extension to other classes.

r6.note: Evidence level D, at the practice cap.
